what:
Block errors UX priorities (from user 2026-04-20, for P1.18 exploration):

1. **Stop hook "returned blocking error" wording is the top issue.** Claude Code renders Stop hook blocks with language that makes users think something is broken. Users may think the tool errored. Needs reframing — either via Claude Code output shape changes, an Anthropic feature request, or user-facing explanation so people don't panic. This is the #1 block-errors UX concern.

2. **Soft blocks lack visibility.** When hooks return additionalContext (soft nudge), the prompt isn't surfaced to the user — only the agent sees it. User thinks it would be helpful if users could also see the soft-nudge prompt (opt-in or default?) so they understand why the agent is calling aide_recall/aide_search.

Explore fixes in BOTH directions: hide/soften the alarming "error" label on Stop blocks, and ADD visibility for soft nudges.
why: User-specified direction on UX exploration task. Previous spec notes covered the labeling inconsistency generically; user clarified the specific concerns: Stop hook "blocking error" language (primary fear factor) and soft-block invisibility (primary missed-opportunity).
